title: Having "Awake" aktivated makes my laptop need a hard reset in the morning

judgment.rationale: The report already narrows the symptom to Awake being enabled but passive, and it includes a bug-report ZIP, but a hard-reset overnight crash still needs OS crash evidence and a current-build confirmation before PowerToys can be blamed or fixed safely.
evidence: The reporter says the laptop crashes overnight only when Awake is enabled, even when Awake is set to follow the normal power plan, and that turning the module off completely stops the recurring problem.
The issue already includes a PowerToysReport ZIP plus detailed hardware, Windows build, and install-scope information.
`src/modules/awake/Awake/Core/Manager.cs` computes active keep-awake execution-state flags only for non-passive modes and `ReapplyAwakeState()` returns early when `CurrentOperatingMode` is `PASSIVE`.
There are no comments or linked fixes that identify whether the overnight hard reset is a PowerToys-owned passive-mode bug or a deeper OS/driver/firmware crash path.
judgment.recommended_action: Request crash-time Event Viewer evidence plus a latest-stable A/B confirmation for Awake Off versus Awake passive mode.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report names the right module, but the current public evidence does not isolate a PowerToys code path strongly enough to justify a fix proposal without crash-time OS evidence.

issue_context.summary: The reporter already did useful narrowing: the machine reportedly hard-resets overnight only when Awake is left enabled, even in follow-normal-power-plan mode. Because passive Awake should not assert keep-awake flags, the next discriminating evidence is crash-time OS data and current-build confirmation rather than another generic bug-report request.
known_information: The issue is on PowerToys 0.99.1 using auto-update, targeting the Awake module.
The laptop is a Lenovo P16s on Windows 11 Pro 25H2 build 26200.8875, and the reporter says the problem stops when Awake is fully turned off from the tray.
A PowerToysReport ZIP is already attached.
There are no public maintainer comments or linked fixes on the thread.
inferences: Because passive Awake should not continually request `ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED`, the overnight hard reset may involve a deeper power-event interaction than ordinary keep-awake mode logic.
A fresh current-build comparison between Awake Off and Awake Passive could quickly separate an old-build issue from a still-current regression.
issue_context.analysis: This is not a good place for a speculative fix. The reporter already provided more than the average Awake issue, but a motherboard-reset-level overnight crash still needs OS crash signatures to establish ownership. The narrowest next step is crash-time Event Viewer data plus a simple current-build comparison of Awake Off versus Passive.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full issue body and noted the existing PowerToysReport ZIP and detailed hardware/Windows information.

Inspected `src/modules/awake/Awake/Core/Manager.cs` and confirmed passive mode early-returns from `ReapplyAwakeState()` and does not compute active keep-awake flags the same way as indefinite/timed modes.
Inspected `src/modules/awake/Awake.ModuleServices/AwakeService.cs` and confirmed the current service model explicitly distinguishes Passive, Indefinite, Timed, and Expirable states.

comment.body:
Thanks for already attaching a PowerToys report and for narrowing this to **Awake enabled but following the normal power plan**.

**Needed**
1. Please confirm whether this still reproduces on the latest stable PowerToys build.
2. Please compare two overnight runs with the rest of the setup unchanged: one with **Awake fully Off**, and one with **Awake enabled but in passive / follow-normal-power-plan mode**, and tell us whether only the passive-Awake run crashes.
3. After the next failing reboot, please open **Event Viewer > Windows Logs > System** and **Application** and share the entries from the crash time, especially any **BugCheck**, **Kernel-Power**, **WHEA**, or **Application Error** events.
4. If it still reproduces on the current build, please submit a comment containing `/bugreport` right after Windows becomes usable again, or run `BugReportTool.exe` if the normal UI cannot open.

This will tell us whether the hard reset is tied to PowerToys' passive Awake process or to a broader OS/driver crash path.
